 Judgment

In this appeal, the petitioner has challenged the judgment and award dated 24.03.2017 in M.V.C.No.699/2016 passed by the V Addl. District and Sessions Judge and Addl. M.A.C.T.,
Shivamogga, Sitting at Sagar ('the Tribunal' for short).
2.
For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 30.11.2015 at about 11:00 am while the petitioner being the pillion rider, riding motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-15/W- 0762, met with an accident near Nadakalasi Bus Stand of Sagar-Sorab Road, sustaining the injuries.
After taking treatment, he approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-.
Claim was opposed by the respondents.
The Tribunal after taking the evidence, awarded the compensation of Rs.1,77,000/- with 6% interest p.a.
Pleading NC: 2024:KHC:1858 inadequacy and seeking enhancement, the petitioner has filed this appeal on various grounds.

4. Heard the arguments of Smt. V. Vetri Lakshmi, learned counsel on behalf of Sri. Vasanthappa,
learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri. Pruthvi Wodeyar, learned counsel for respondent No.1 and Sri. K. Sridhara, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
5.
It is the contention of learned counsel for the petitioner PW-2

Dr. Chethan has given evidence that the petitioner has suffered 10% whole body disability, but the Tribunal ignored the same; taken the income at Rs.6,000/- as against notional income at Rs.9,000/- assessed in the year 2015;
compensation awarded under different heads is inadequate and she sought for enhancement.

It is further contended that for the rider not holding valid driving licence, petitioner cannot be penalized,
the Insurance Company has to deposit and then recover NC: 2024:KHC:1858 from the owner of the motor cycle by applying the principles laid down in National Insurance Co. Ltd.
-Vs.- Swaran Singh and Others 1 and Pappu and Others -Vs.- Vinod Kumar Lamba and Another2.
6.

Learned counsel for the insured has contended that the Tribunal has correctly assessed the compensation, there is no need for enhancement; facial injury will not cause any physical disability and he supported the impugned judgment.

7. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the compensation assessed is proportionate to the gravity of the injury and money spent towards treatment, there is no need for enhancement, the Tribunal has rightly dismissed the claim against the Insurance Company,

8. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and also perused the materials on record.
9. The material on record did point out that on 13.11.2015, the petitioner being the pillion rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-15/W-0762, met with an accident and suffered various injuries.

Ex.P16/wound certificate and also evidence of PW-2 Dr. Chethan, points out the following injuries sustained by the petitioner:
i) Swelling and disfiguration of face.
ii) Fracture of body of mandible 'U' displaced fracture of hard palate.
iii) Fracture of anterior and lateral wall of bilateral maxillary sinuses, medial and lateral wall of bilateral orbit, Bilateral nasal bone fracture.
iv) Small acute subarchnoid bleed.
Small pocket of free air in bilateral orbital extra coral space.
Fracture of left zygomatic arch.

NC: 2024:KHC:1858 The treated Doctor, though spoken about 10% disability, having regard to agricultural work carried out by the petitioner, the injury may cause discomfort and loss of amenites only and it is not a case for assessment of disability.

10. The Tribunal assessed the compensation as follows:
 Sl. No. Particulars Rs.
 1 Pain and suffering 40,000  2 Loss of income during 12,000  treatment period  3
Medical expenses 92,000  4 Loss of future amenities 20,000  5
Attendant charges 8,000
6 Nourishment, diet and 5,000  conveyance  Total 1,77,000 11.
The petitioner has no proof of income being an Agriculturist.
Even if he is considered as a person with no proof of income, notional income will be assessed at Rs.9,000/- in the year 2015 as against Rs.6,000/- assessed by the Tribunal.
The Tribunal NC: 2024:KHC:1858 has not considered the future medical expenses and awarded lesser compensation towards loss of amenities and discomfort.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled to:-
Sl. No. Particulars

Rs . 
 1 Pain and sufferings 40,000 Parashuram vs Noorulla on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77491370/
3  2 Loss of income during laid-up 18,000  for 2 months (Rs.9,000/- x 2)
 3
Medical expenses 92,000  4 Attendant charges and 8,000  travelling expenses
5 Food and nourishment 5,000  6 Loss of amenities and 40,000  discomfort  7
Future medical expenses 5,000  Total 2,08,000
Total compensation comes to Rs.2,08,000/- as against Rs.1,77,000/-, thereby enhancement of Rs.31,000/-.
This is the just compensation that the petitioner is entitled to in the facts and circumstances of the case.

12. As regarding liability is concerned, the petitioner is relying the judgments in Swaran Singh's case (supra) and Pappu's case (supra) NC: 2024:KHC:1858 to plead that pay and recovery has to be ordered.
Admittedly there is no evidence on record to explain that the rider did possess valid driving license at the time of accident.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Singh Ram -Vs.- Nirmala and Ors.3, in a similar situation where the Tribunal absolved the Insurance Company from its liability to indemnify the owner for the reason of driver did not possess valid driving licence, directed the Insurance Company to pay the compensation and recover it from the owner of the offending vehicle.

13. In Singh Ram's case (supra), the Hon'ble Apex Court while dealing with the owner, who placed fake driving licence and later a lapsed driving licence renewed after its expiry, referring to the case of Swaran Singh's case (supra), directed the Insurance Company to pay and recover the compensation amount.

The principle of 'pay and recovery' has been settled by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pappu's case (supra) wherein it is held that, the insurer has to satisfy the award and recover it from the insured in case of violation of policy conditions.
In view of the settled law the finding recorded by the Tribunal cannot stand to its reasoning, it needs modification to this effect.
Hence, the insurer has to satisfy the award and recover the same from the insured.
Hence, the appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed-in-part.
(ii) Impugned judgment and award is modified.

4 (iii) The petitioner would be entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.31,000/-
along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the enhanced compensation from the date of petition till its realization, excluding - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:1858 interest for the delayed period of 587 days in filing the appeal and on future medical expenses of Rs.5,000/-.
(iv) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment and further recover it from the insured in the same proceedings.
(v) The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal along with records forthwith.
